entry.summary: Visa-free short stays as part of the Schengen area.
entry.max_stay: 90 days in any 180-day period across the Schengen area
entry.pre_arrival: None today. ETIAS is on the watch list.
entry.other: Apply for any visa in Australia before you go. France Diplomacy has an online visa checker. Schengen Entry/Exit System: fingerprints and photo at the border on first entry (free, nothing to do beforehand). Get an entry stamp where one is still given, and carry your passport across internal borders.

tourism.detail: Australian ordinary passports are normally visa-exempt for short Schengen stays, subject to the 90/180 rule and border conditions.
tourism.next: Run the official France-Visas and Schengen checks immediately before departure.

meetings.route: Short-stay business visitor or conference delegate
meetings.detail: Meetings, negotiations, trade fairs and conference attendance can fit a short professional visit when no French employment or service delivery is performed.
meetings.next: Carry the host letter, schedule, business purpose and proof of funds; do not call a speaking engagement mere attendance.

conference.detail: A delegate, exhibitor or visitor route is distinct from delivering paid programme content or hands-on training.
conference.next: Ask the organiser whether you are attendee, panellist, speaker, trainer or performer and reclassify the route if it changes.

unpaid-speaking.route: Host and consular classification; occasional invited teaching may be exempt
unpaid-speaking.detail: France-Visas identifies occasional teaching by invited professors and short cultural/scientific events as fact-dependent exceptions; a free talk is not automatically outside work rules.
unpaid-speaking.next: Send the exact no-fee arrangement, reimbursements, host status and dates to the host and French mission.

paid-speaking.route: French work authorisation with short-stay or talent route
paid-speaking.detail: Paid speaking, consulting and training are active professional services. Short assignments may use event or temporary-work formalities; longer or high-profile work can use talent passport categories.
paid-speaking.next: Have the French host determine whether an authorisation, exemption, convention or talent passport applies before advertising dates.

book-launch.route: Publisher/venue invitation plus the accurate professional or cultural route
book-launch.detail: Rights meetings can be business travel; a paid reading, signing, workshop, ticketed appearance or local book sales can add work, artist or tax questions.
book-launch.next: Separate author appearance, royalties, fee, merchandise and retail in the invitation.

ai-teaching.route: Invited-researcher/teacher or short professional work route
ai-teaching.detail: A university convention may support research or higher-education teaching; commercial training normally needs the work pathway instead.
ai-teaching.next: Ask the institution to issue the correct convention or work-authorisation documents.

remote-work.route: No broad French digital-nomad visa; visitor or residence classification must be confirmed
remote-work.detail: France has talent and self-employed residence routes but no simple all-purpose remote-worker visa. Foreign remote work while visiting can raise tax, residence and activity questions.
remote-work.next: Confirm the intended duration, employer/client location and French customer activity with a French mission or adviser.

entrepreneur.route: Talent passport creator/investor, entrepreneur or self-employed route
entrepreneur.detail: France-Visas publishes creator, investor, researcher and internationally recognised talent categories with project, qualification or investment evidence.
entrepreneur.next: Choose the exact talent or entrepreneur category and build the French project dossier before relocating.

trade.route: Short professional business visit; local operation needs French business/work status
trade.detail: Sourcing, negotiation, trade fairs and contract discussions can be visitor activity; installing, selling directly or fulfilling locally can become work.
trade.next: Map who invoices, who delivers and where the service occurs.

artist.route: Short cultural event classification or talent passport artist route
artist.detail: Paid or contracted performance, literary work and artistic production have specific French categories; the talent passport cultural profession route is designed for longer engagements.
artist.next: Have the producer specify contracts, dates, royalties, venue licence and whether the engagement is salaried or independent.

mixed-mission.route: Split the France itinerary into Schengen visit, professional delivery and any talent/residence layer
mixed-mission.detail: The quickest route may be visa-free entry while the activation key is a host contract, work authorisation, convention or talent passport.
mixed-mission.next: Give the host one schedule showing every activity, payment, audience and venue.

filming.route: Visa-free Schengen short stay (journalistic or media purposes)
filming.detail: Journalistic or media purposes are listed among visa-free purposes; paid production work and location permits are national matters.
filming.next: Ask the Embassy of France, Yarralumla about filming, and the local authority about locations.

research.route: Visa-free Schengen short stay (short-term study or training)
research.detail: Short-term study and training are covered; paid research at an institution is paid activity.
research.next: Ask the Embassy of France, Yarralumla if the host pays you.

volunteering.detail: Volunteering isn't addressed in the EU guidance read.
volunteering.next: Ask the Embassy of France, Yarralumla.

laws.rule: You must always carry a photo ID, such as your passport or driver's licence. Police conduct random checks, particularly at borders. It's illegal not to offer help to a person in danger. Authorities may charge you if you: don't stop after you witness a motor accident don't report an accident to emergency services ignore pleas for help or urgent assistance. Any assistance shouldn't put you or anyone else in danger. For example, if there's a fire, you're not expected to leap into the flames to save someone. Notifying authorities (dial 112) would be sufficient. Penalties for not assisting can carry a fine of up to 100,000 euros and up to 7 years imprisonment. Tourists aren't exempt. Forcing some

laws.rule: You'll need a valid Australian driver's licence to drive. Car rental companies may also need an International Driving Permit (IDP) in addition to your driver's license (the IDP alone is insufficient). You should get your IDP before you leave Australia. Otherwise, you can apply for an IDP online and have it shipped internationally for a fee. If you live in France, you can swap your Australian driver's licence for a French licence. You must do this within your first 12 months.

money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: The currency in France is the Euro. France is a member of the European Union (EU). If you travel between France and any non-EU country, you must declare over 10,000 euros (or equivalent) cash. This covers all forms of currency, not only cash. If you don't declare or give the wrong information on entry or exit, you'll need to pay a fine. You don't need to declare cash if you're travelling to or from another EU country.

visa-preparation.fastest_entry: Visa-free short stays (90 days or less) as part of the Schengen area, in some cases.
visa-preparation.before_departure: Nothing to lodge before travel today: EES registration happens at the border. ETIAS hadn't started on 2026-11-01.
steps: France is in the Schengen area: short stays of 90 days or less can be visa-free in some cases; other purposes or longer stays need a visa before travel.
At the first Schengen border, give fingerprints and a photo for the Entry/Exit System (EES). It's free; nothing is needed before arrival, and sites charging for it are fraudulent.
Carry your passport when crossing borders, including inside Schengen (temporary internal checks are in place in places).
Visas must be applied for in Australia; status can't be changed once in France. France Diplomacy has an online visa tool.
